role: primitive ES (gcd(x, y, z) = 1) as a sharper sibling of (★)
missing_theorem: PROVED here (elementary): for primes p ≡ 1 (4), Type I solutions are never primitive, and every Type II solution is (abk, pkma, pkmb) with gcd(a, b) = 1, m | a + b, p = 4abk − (a+b)/m, gcd(x, y, z) = k. So the primitive solutions are exactly k = 1: p = 4ab − (a+b)/m. (★) is the dual line m = 1 (k = C). (a, m) = (1, 1) gives p = 3b − 1, so every p ≡ 2 (mod 3) has a primitive solution; this explains 'all failures ≡ 1 (mod 12)'. Missing theorem: every large prime p ≡ 1 (12) has coprime a, b and m | a + b with p = 4ab − (a+b)/m.

Pass 1 U04: 110 failures ≤ 10⁵, 56 of them ≤ 2·10⁴ (density thinning).
barrier: B2 (single-integer lottery with a smaller mean); B2 Thm 2.2(iii) does not apply (infinitely many slices)

role: Hilbert property / thin images for integral points of n: 𝒰 → A¹ (Corvaja–Zannier)
missing_theorem: A thin-image theorem explaining Mordell–Schinzel (identity families miss square classes) and describing what a covering family must look like.
status_ref: Pass 1 U04 (no such statement in the CZ framework). GEOMETRY_ES §1: over ℚ (indeed over ℤ[1/n]) x = nX identifies U_n ≅ U_1, so every geometric/Galois invariant is independent of n; n enters only through the integral model: the fibration is isotrivial over ℚ, so Hilbert-property questions about rational points are trivial; the square-class phenomenon is about integral models (T1 is a Hilbert-reciprocity statement, (J)13).
note: Mordell–Schinzel is not a thin-set phenomenon of the generic fibre.

status_ref: FRONTIER §3 B-fin; this pass (Z0865); final_checks.json

role: rational vs integral points on the ES cubic (where integrality is lost)
missing_theorem: None beyond the scaling principle: GEOMETRY_ES §1: over ℚ (indeed over ℤ[1/n]) x = nX identifies U_n ≅ U_1, so every geometric/Galois invariant is independent of n; n enters only through the integral model. ES(n) ⟺ U_1 has a positive rational point with denominators dividing n. Integrality is lost exactly in the denominators, which is the divisor lottery.
status_ref: GEOMETRY_ES §1–2 (s-form); BRAINSTORM/rational_to_integral_cubic.md

role: local densities of U_p at primes dividing 2p and across residue classes of p

role: Fourier control of a digit-like thin set of p (Maynard) intersecting the ES-good set

status_ref: Pass 1 U04: the uncovered set mod 840·k is the square-class set (a union of residue classes, a group-like set with large Fourier coefficients, not a digit set); B1: covered vs uncovered is congruence data, and ES at primes in the uncovered classes is the lottery.
note: Maynard's method needs a set with small Fourier mass; square classes are the opposite.

role: Gross–Hacking–Keel theta functions on the Looijenga pair of U_n

status_ref: Pass 1 H07: theta functions give regular functions, not integral points; in the flagship GHK example (Markoff cubics) integral Hasse fails infinitely often with non-empty BM set (Loughran–Mitankin, Ghosh–Sarnak), so 'canonical positive structure ⇒ integral points' is false in the closest case. GEOMETRY_ES §1: over ℚ (indeed over ℤ[1/n]) x = nX identifies U_n ≅ U_1, so every geometric/Galois invariant is independent of n; n enters only through the integral model.

Pass 1 U04 (discussed in B2_ACROSS_FIELDS, s9_fibration_level).
